before_times: Where did the water come from, and when?
Is it clean water, toilet water, or flood or sewage water?
Is water near outlets, lights or the electrical panel?
Is the water still coming, or is it shut off?
Which rooms are wet, and about how big?
Mold already seen? About how big?
Fire or smoke: is the fire department done, and may you go back in?
after_time: Do you have insurance for this? (yes or no only; the details go on the secure page)
The year the home was built (before 1978: lead-safe work where the state's rules require it)
Anything to know at the door, like parking, pets or a key for the daily checks
secure_page_only: Own or rent; a renter forwards a link to the owner
The insurer, the policy number and the deductible
A key box or door code for the daily checks
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older). A renter can book water removal; only the owner, or someone the owner allows, OKs cutting out walls, ceilings or floors.

stop: sparks, a burning smell, or live wires in water
a ceiling or wall giving way
a fire still burning, or the fire department not done

go_on.water near outlets, lights or the panel: Stay out of that room, and don't touch switches while standing in water. Call the power company to cut the power; 911 for sparks. The booking goes on, marked urgent.
go_on.sewage: Keep children and pets out, don't touch it bare-handed, and stop flushing and running water. The booking goes on, marked sewage, so the crew brings protective gear.
go_on.a wet ceiling bulging near a light: Stay out of the room and don't touch the switch. Turn that breaker off only if the panel is dry and you're not standing in water.

safety_and_stop_words.always: The general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency means call 911, and no booking.

what_rosie_says.rising water or someone trapped: Call 911 now and get to higher ground. Never walk or drive through floodwater. Nothing is booked until everyone is safe.
what_rosie_says.gas, sparks or burning: Get out, then call 911 and the utility. Nothing is booked.
what_rosie_says.a ceiling giving way: Stay out of that room, and call 911 if anyone is hurt.

prep: Stop the water at the main valve if it's safe.
Photograph everything wet before anything is moved, for your insurer.
Move small things off wet floors; leave heavy wet rugs for the crew.
Report it to your insurer today, if you're insured.
At the shop: bring wet photos and papers in a sealed bag or box; don't pull stuck photos apart.
required: Every job at the customer's place: the work authorization, signed on the secure page while the time is saved. It names the work allowed, the price list, who pays, stop-anytime and the cancel terms. It's kept with that job only.
A renter's job that cuts out walls, ceilings or floors: the owner signs on a link the renter forwards. Water removal can start before that.
Mold of the size the state's rules license: a written plan from another company first, and the state told before the start, where its rules require it.
Smoke and soot cleaning priced from photos: a written estimate, signed before the deposit.

skills: Mold removal: only licensed workers, where the state licenses it
Contents: photos, papers, rugs and soft goods (the shop)
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Mold removal workers hold their own license where the state's rules require one. A lead-safe certified renovator goes where work disturbs paint in a home built before 1978, where the rules require it.
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs prices over $500 made for one customer. Pat may OK them too; Sam's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: A stand-in crew needs the same skill (and license for mold). A new crew at the door is offered first, never assumed.
staff.crews: An emergency goes to a crew lead, who brings a helper.
staff.on_call: Sam sets who takes sent-now jobs in open hours and who's on call at night, on weekends and holidays, each with a backup crew. The one on call gets urgent texts at any hour and takes a job by reply within 5 minutes; then the backup.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older). A renter can book water removal; only the owner, or someone the owner allows, OKs cutting out walls, ceilings or floors.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A teen can't book; a parent books.

visit.check_in: The check-in code at the door. Then, before any work, the lead checks the signer matches the work authorization, the power, and the kind and source of the water.
visit.done: The code on the first visit, then DONE when the last spot reads dry and the machines are picked up.
visit.changes_at_visit: The scope is priced from the signed list and OK'd by the customer before any work. Dirtier water than said, or more rooms wet, is shown as new lines first. A renter's walls wait for the owner's OK; the water comes out anyway.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Water and fire cleanup: a contractor's license or registration only where the state's form asks for one; elsewhere identity is checked, and 'license: what the business says'. Mold removal: where the state licenses it, a license for the business and one for each worker. Contents cleaning at the shop: none, the business registration only.
license.who: The business, and for mold removal each worker too, as the state's form says.
license.ask: The company's number at sign-up; each person's own number with their invite reply.
license.insurance: Asked where the state's form needs it.
